characters.name: Spartacus
characters.description: Spartacus (real name unknown) is a Thracian warrior who becomes a famous gladiator in the arena, later to build a legend upon himself during the Third Servile War. For the first season, he served as a gladiator in Batiatus' Ludus under the direction of Doctore and rivaled the then-Champion of Capua, Crixus. Later, he and many of the gladiators broke free from captivity and began an armed rebellion against Rome. The Ace: He establishes himself as one inBlood and Sand. He not only becomes the top gladiator at the ludus, but is a brilliant military tactician and a charismatic leader (not to mentionquite good in bed, apparently). Animal Motifs: Theserpent. Arc Symbol: The red serpent that Sura mentioned to him. Also the rain. Asskicking Leads to Leadership: After heslays Sedullusthe Germans quickly fall into line and recognise that he is the one in charge.

characters.name: Doctore Oenomaus
characters.description: Oenomaus is the gladiator trainer in Batiatus' Ludus, traditionally referred to only by the title of "Doctore". At a young age, he was recruited into the ludus by former lanista Titus Batiatus, whom he came to see as a father figure. After the downfall of the House of Batiatus, Oenomaus believed he had lost his purpose in the world and retired himself to die in The Pit. However, with the help of Spartacus and the other Rebels, he eventually finds a new purpose and joins the Rebels' cause, quickly being recognized as a mentor. He was married to Melitta before her death. Animal Motifs:The stallion. Asskicking Leads to Leadership: New recruits are quick to learn this. Even Spartacus recognizes that Oenomaus is the only person in the ludus that could actually stop him from leaving. Badass Teacher: To the gladiators and later to the rebels. Bald of Authority: In the first season and late in the prequel season. Becomes this to rebels (though second-in-command to Spartacus) late in the second season.

characters.name: Crixus
characters.description: Crixus is the former Champion of Capua, introduced into Batiatus' Ludus as a slave desiring the life of a gladiator, whom eventually fights his way up to become one of the top gladiators of the ludus. During the arrival of Spartacus in Blood and Sand, Crixus is seen as champion and becomes the lover of Naevia. Always Save the Girl: IfNaeviais in trouble, he'll do anything and everything to save her, regardless of the long-term effects on the others or himself. This tends tobackfire; in the first season, when he realises Ashur raped Naevia by tauntingly groping her in front of him, he attacks him...in front ofeveryonein the ludus, thus revealing he and Naevia'sSecret Relationship(andplaying right into Ashur's hands, he having deliberately done this to set Crixus off). InVengeance, Crixus's main motivation for the first half of the season is finding Naevia at any costs and leads what is effectively aSuicide Missioninto the mines to rescue her, resulting inmany deaths and Crixus getting captured. Animal Motifs: The octopus. Arc Symbol: Tiberius' sword in the final season. Asskicking Leads to Leadership: As you might imagine, the gladiatorial champion of Capua got there by kicking lots and lots andlotsof ass.

characters.name: Varro
characters.description: Varro is a gladiator in the house of Batiatus. He was once a free Roman man, but voluntarily became a gladiator in Batiatus' ludus to pay off his momentous gambling debts. He rose from being a common recruit to becoming one of the more formidable gladiators in the ludus. Varro is the husband of Aurelia, father of Janus, and a friend to Spartacus. Action Dad: To his young son, Janus. Animal Motifs:The eel. Ascended Fanboy: Played with. Varro is a fan of gladiators who eventually becomes one; however, in this context it means that he lost so much money gambling on fights that he wasMade a Slavein order to pay his debts. Bash Brothers: With Spartacus.

characters.name: Sura
characters.description: Sura is Spartacus' Thracian wife and inspiration, tragically taken from him after he deserts from the Roman auxiliary by his most hated enemy, Gaius Claudius Glaber. Action Girl: She can handle a sword and does a good job holding off four or five armed attackers before Spartacus shows up to help. When plotting his escape, Spartacus considers her combat ability an asset to get by the guards. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Subverted: Spartacus isThe Hedonistwhen they firsthad sex. However, it turns out she didn't do it because he was a bad boy, but because the gods had shown her that, once he fell for her, he would bea fantastic guy. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She is composed and quitesnarky, with dark brown hair. Always Someone Better: She's considered this by Mira, Spartacus'Second Loveinterest. Although she respects Spartacus' continued love for his deceased wife, she clearly feels hurt and increasingly resentful that Spartacus cannot love her as deeply as he loves Sura. Spartacus's third love interest Laeta seems to feel this way about Sura too, but to a far lesser extent; she's not as insecure about it as Mira and is more understandingprobably because she also knows what it's like to lose a spouse.

characters.name: Naevia
characters.description: Naevia is a former slave in the House of Batiatus, owned by Lucretia, who later becomes Crixus' love interest. She is banished from the Ludus after their love affair is discovered. She is eventually found by the Rebels, and joins their cause alongside her lover. Action Survivor: InVengeance, she's able to survive a number of life-threatening situations despite being a handmaiden her whole life and starts learning how to defend herself properly, culminating in hernarrowly defeating Ashur in a sword fight. She eventually graduates toDark Action Girl. Affectionate Pickpocket: She steals a key to the gate separating the gladiator cells from the villa by flirting with a guard, in order to be with Crixus. However, Crixus sees them together and assumes Naevia's affections have turned from himuntil she explains what she was really doing. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: Mostly only towards Crixus in the first season, until theirRelationship Upgrade. She becomes a straighter example in the third season. Ambiguously Brown: More so when played by Lesley-Ann Brandt, who has mixed ancestry (Cynthia Addai-Robinson was more clearly black, though she is also mixed race). Naevia is said to be Phoenician, who originated from the Eastern Mediterranean.

characters.name: Mira
characters.description: Mira is a former house slave serving Lucretia in the House of Batiatus. She helps Spartacus during his uprising, becomes a fighter, and later becomes his love interest during the beginning stages of the Third Servile War. Action Girl: Especially inVengeance, after she receives formal combat training. Action Survivor: Initially one, until shegets proper training in the second season. All Love Is Unrequited: Played with. She falls in love with Spartacus and they enter a relationship. However, although Spartacus cares for Mira and respects her, he isstill not over his wifeand does not fully return Mira's feelings, to her disappointment. They eventually break up because of it. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: Mostly inBlood and Sand. She becomes friendly inVengeance.

characters.name: Agron
characters.description: One of the later recruits to Batiatus' Ludus, Agron is a skilled fighter and one of Spartacus' chief lieutenants during the rebellion. Never having been fond of the Romans in the first place, Agron harbors a visceral hatred towards the Romans ever since he lost his brother Duro during the upheaval at Batiatus' ludus. Agron is fond of and loyal to Spartacus. After the death of his brother, he goes on to become the lover of Nasir. Adaptation Name Change: Ultimately subverted as Castus appeared in the final season. Aloof Big Brother: Averted in that he doesn't seem to be aloof at all; if anything, his temper isworsethan his brother's, and his major story inBlood and Sanddeals with him learning to stop being so overprotective of Duro. Animal Motifs:The crab. Badass Long Robe: On occasion inVengeance.

characters.name: Barca
characters.description: He is one of the top gladiators in Batiatus' Ludus, becoming famously known as the Beast of Carthage after (reputedly) defeating his father Mago in the arena. He is the lover of Auctus, and later Pietros. Always Someone Better: He is never the best gladiator for Batiatus, always only ever second best to: Oenomaus, Gannicus, Crixus, and Spartacus. Anti-Villain:Type II and sometimes Type I. The Big Guy: One of the tallest gladiators. The Brute: Was this to Batiatus; he never had any real authority, but served as Batiatus' bodyguard and hitman.

characters.name: Aurelia
characters.description: Aurelia is a Roman woman and wife to Varro. She becomes a slave in order to pay off her late husband's debts, but is later freed during the revolt. Spartacus then sends her away, although with unexpected consequences. Action Survivor: While not a trained fighter, she did castrate her rapist when he attacked a second time, and stabs Numerius to death as revenge for ordering Varro's execution. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: Despite theHair Color Dissonance, it's still pretty dark. Beware the Nice Ones: Shecastratedher rapist and brutally killed the person who ordered her husband's death. Break the Cutie: Her husband had to sell himself into slavery to pay off his gambling debts, then she got knocked up by a rapist; her beloved husband rejected her for it and took her back just in time to die at an exhibition, not even in the arena, leading to her having to become a slave as well. Her arc ends when the Romans capture and torture her; although the rebels rescue her, she winds up dying of her injuries.

characters.name: Medicus
characters.description: Medicus is the devoted and skilled doctor for the House of Batiatus, tending the injured Gladiators after their many battles. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": Is only ever referred to by his job title. Put on a Bus: Disappears after the destruction of Batiatus and his villa.

characters.name: Pietros
characters.description: Pietros is a slave in Batiatus' Ludus, serving the gladiators and as Doctore's assistant of sorts. He is the lover of Barca. Because You Were Nice to Me: The main reason why Spartacus lost it whenhe committed suicide and killed Gnaeus for mocking it. Break the Cutie: Lied to by his lover whodies tragically, raped by Gnaeus not so long after, and finallyDriven to Suicide. Butt-Monkey: Eventually becomes one. And none of it's played for laughs. Driven to Suicide:After experiencing one hell of aTrauma Conga Line(he was tricked into believing his lover abandoned him and them continually raped and abused by Gnaeus) he can't take it anymore and hangs himself.

characters.name: Duro
characters.description: Duro is a Germanic gladiator serving in the ludus of Batiatus. His brother, Agron, also serves Batiatus as a gladiator. Always Second Best: To Agron as part of theirSibling Team. He loves his brother, but feels humiliated at constantly needing to be protected by him. Bash Brothers: With his older brother, Agron. Dies Wide Open: Well, half-open. Due to the Dead: One of the fallen characters honored inThe Dead and the Dying.

characters.name: Segovax
characters.description: Segovax is a Gaul slave bought by Batiatus in the markets to train in Batiatus' Ludus and was put under Illithiya's patronage. Anti-Villain: Becomes this in his desperation for freedom. Apologetic Attacker: Apologies to a victim while strangling him. Cruel and Unusual Death: Aside from getting crucified, he was also castrated. Even the Guys Want Him: Agron took a peek at hisGag Penis, which is likely the firstForeshadowingof his sexuality.

characters.name: Rhaskos
characters.description: Rhaskos is a gladiator in Batiatus' Ludus. He joins Spartacus and the other freed slaves in seeking vengeance, and becomes one of the more prominent rebels. The Big Guy: He's portrayed as something of a brute compared to Crixus. Due to the Dead: One of the fallen characters honored inThe Dead and the Dying. Jerk Jock: One of many bullies among the Gauls, and continues to be so after the slaves rebel. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Well, gold is a little strong, but he's not a total jerk.

characters.name: Gnaeus
characters.description: Gnaeus is a Dacian slave and gladiator in the house of Batiatus. Asshole Victim: He definitely had it coming. Berserk Button: He doesn't take the mocking of his fighting-style well. Bullying a Dragon: He mocks Spartacus over Pietros's death when Spartacus is a better fighter and Gnaeus is standing near the edge of a cliff. He clearly thinks Batiatus's favor will save him. It doesn't. Butt-Monkey: He gets constantly humiliated throughout the series.

characters.name: Rabanus
characters.description: Rabanus is a Sardinian rebel and former gladiator in the House of Batiatus. Cruel and Unusual Death: Crucified in theGrand Finale. Identical Stranger: To Rhaskos.

characters.name: The Veteran
characters.description: The Veteran is a Greek slave and former gladiator for Batiatus, and later a rebel under Spartacus' command.

characters.name: Hamilcar
characters.description: Hamilcar is one of several gladiators in Batiatus' Ludus. Butt-Monkey: According toThe Other Wiki, he never won a single battle. At least on screen. Forgotten Fallen Friend: One of the few fallen characters who wasn't honored inThe Dead and the Dying. Informed Ability: After Gnaeus becomes unfit to fight Crixus in the Primus, Doctore and Batiatus settle for him as replacement before Spartacus asserted himself. Many argue that the likes of Barca and Rhaskos are the better replacements, if not the better first choice. Jerk Jock: Said the page quote to Spartacus after being condemned to the pit.

characters.name: Kerza
characters.description: Kerza is one of several gladiators in Batiatus' Ludus. Badass Boast: Desperately trying not to show fear when going to the pits, claims that he willFUCK! THEM! ALL!. Butt-Monkey: Gets the shit beaten out of him in the Ludus and killed in the pits. Forgotten Fallen Friend: One of the few fallen characters who wasn't honored inThe Dead and the Dying, but nobody really liked him, anyway. Groin Attack: On the receiving end of one for laughing at one of Doctore's statements in his speech to the newly recruited gladiators.

characters.name: Gannicus
characters.description: Gannicus serves as champion in Batiatus' Ludus throughout the events of the prequel,Gods of the Arena, until his departure upon earning his freedom in the aftermath of the Games of the New Arena. He later returns inVengeanceinitially as an acquaintance to the rebels, criticizing their cause against the Roman Republic, though he ironically becomes a rebel himself for the sake of his closest friend, Oenomaus. The Ace: Gradually deconstructed into aBroken Acein the prequel, though it starts getting reconstructed during the final season. Age-Gap Romance: His romance with Sibyl. While there's only a six year age difference between their actors, Sibyl is supposed to be about twenty, while Gannicus is a grizzled veteran who is at least ten years older. The Alcoholic: Rarely seen without wine.He states that he's lost his taste for it after falling in love with Sibyl. Almighty Janitor: Inverted. Spartacus actually wants him to be an officialRebel Leader, but Gannicus insists on just being another sword.He finally complies in the finale.

characters.name: Melitta
characters.description: Melitta is the wife of Oenomaus and servant in Batiatus' Ludus, serving as Lucretia's body slave. Accidental Murder: Poor Melitta. She'saccidentally poisoned by Lucretia, after stealing and drinking from an amphora of wine Lucretia had slipped poison into without her knowledge. All-Loving Heroine: She is compassionate and helpful towards everyone, in particular being very warm and supportive towards her husband and Gannicus, acting asa mother figureto the younger slaves and even showing kindness and sympathy towardsLucretia(although this was when she wasless evil than she becamebyBlood & Sand). Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She is the most mature and levelheaded of the house slaves, who look up to her. Ambiguously Brown: She's played by a Hispanic actress (Marisa Ramirez describes her background as including Mexican, Native American and Irish), with a name that's Greek in origin, and she's a slave in a Roman nation.

characters.name: Diona
characters.description: Diona is one of many slaves who serves Batiatus and Lucretia. She is a close friend of Naevia. All Women Are Lustful: Cruelly subverted. She giggles and gossips about sex and men with her friends, and seems excited at the prospect of losing her virginity.Then she is raped by Cossutius and becomes utterly horrified by the whole prospect, even stating she hopes that the next man who rapes her "takes her life as well". Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She starts out as sweet and innocent, but aftershe is rapedshe becomes colder and more withdrawn, especially towards Naevia. Beautiful Slave Girl: She's an attractive girl who has served the House of Batiatus since childhood. Lucretia initially preserves her virginity so she'll be worth more, but thenreluctantly allows her to be raped by Cossutius to secure favours for her husband. It all goes downhill for Diona from there. Beauty Is Never Tarnished: Averted. After beingrecaptured following a failed escape attempt, she looks terrible - sickly pale with messy hair and chapped lips, and covered in cuts and bruises(apparently frombeing beatenwhen she was captured).

characters.name: Doctore Ulpius
characters.description: Ulpius was the Doctore of Batiatus' ludus before the title was passed on to Oenomaus. He is said to have held the position even during the time of Titus Batiatus. Badass Teacher: Given he's teaching gladiators, this is pretty much required, and he proves it in the second episode. Brutal Honesty: Often does this, though it gets him into trouble withQuintus, who doesn't appreciate him calling him out. Covered with Scars: On his face, at least. Cool Old Guy: He served under Titus (Batiatus' elderly father, is easily one of the oldest gladiators in the ludus and can still kick serious ass.

characters.name: Dagan
characters.description: Dagan is a Syrian slave and gladiator in the House of Batiatus. Breakup Breakout: He became this in his duo with Ashur In-Universe.Unfortunately for him, Ashur doesn't take being theLesser Starwell. The Big Guy: Stands at 6'5. Butt-Monkey: From the fourth episode onwards, things keep going wrong for him (mostly at the hands of Ashur). Defiant to the End:After Ashur stabs him, he gave him a headbutt before succumbing to his wounds.

characters.name: Auctus
characters.description: Auctus is a gladiator in Batiatus' Ludus and former lover of Barca. Blood from the Mouth: AfterCrixus stabs him through the torso. Bury Your Gays: Well, it was something of aForegone Conclusion. Face Death with Dignity: "Barca, has taught you well..." Foregone Conclusion: Autus doesn't appear inBlood and Sandand Barca is with Pietros in that season...

characters.name: Nasir
characters.description: Nasir is a young Syrian slave who is freed by Spartacus' rebellion. During the rebellion, he goes on to become a lethal fighter and the lover of Agron. Action Survivor: At first. Unlike most of Spartacus' group, Nasir was a body slave and never experienced combat or violent hardship like the gladiators. However, he quickly realizes that if he wants to remain in the rebellion, then he needs to learn how to fight and kill Romans. Berserk Button: The one time he gets truly angry at Agron is when he attempts to dictate who he can associate with or what he can do. Cannot Spit It Out: To Agron. They spend a good half of the season dancing around their attraction, even thougheveryone else can see that they like each other. Defeat Means Friendship: With Spartacus and the other rebels. After his attempt to kill Spartacus fails and the latter prevents Agron from killing him, Nasir starts to see that therebels aren't as terrible or misguidedas his Roman masters led him to believe. By the season's end, Nasir is completely loyal to Spartacus and falls in love with Agron.

characters.name: Lucius Caelius
characters.description: Lucius Caelius of the Caelian clan. His family was struck down through the proscription program implemented by Lucius Cornelius Sulla, a prominent Roman politician who achieved consulship in 88 BCE and ruled as Rome's dictator for three years until he retired. The Alcoholic: In his introduction. Badass Teacher: To Mira and some of the other slaves, specifically teaching them how to fight with a bow. Cool Old Guy: Despite his age, he's willing to fight when badly outnumbered and under-equipped. Hunter of His Own Kind: He is Roman, but hates the Republic due to the fact a rival killed his family and stole his lands, whilst the elite did nothing.

characters.name: Chadara
characters.description: Chadara is one of the many slaves that Spartacus and his men have freed. She is unsure of her place among the freed men and women, and attempts to secure a higher position (and protection) by using her body. All Women Are Lustful: A rather tragic example. She uses sex to gain position with the rebel camp and doesn't seem to think she's any good at anything else. Armor-Piercing Response: When a repulsed Mira asks why she would willingly sleep with Rhaskos, who isn't exactly a dreamboat, Chadara replies that being his lover ensures her a safe place among the rebels, as they aren't all as lucky as Mira to have Spartacus' affections and protection. Mira realizes Chadara has a point and it inspires her to learn how to fight properly, and to encourage the others to learn. Asshole Victim: Downplayed. She is killed by accident while trying to sneak away, having stolen the map and significant money. Spartacus and Gannicus were fighting to the death over the assumption that the latter was the thief, and beforehand she had ample opportunity to say she had done it and prevent everything. And the fact that she stole in the first place rather than asking Spartacus or even Mira for help or advice on starting a new life. Canon Foreigner: There are no historical records of an Greek concubine joining Spartacus' resistance.

characters.name: Saxa
characters.description: Saxa is one of a group of Germanic prisoners rescued from a slave ship in Neapolis who become rebels under Spartacus' command. Action Girl: One of the most prominent in the series. Notably, she wasapparentlyalwaysa capable fighter, unlike most of the otherAction Girls, who tend to start out asAction Survivorsbeforetaking levels in badass. Indeed, behind the scenes, Ellen Hollman scored the highest out of all the cast on the fitness tests as part of gladiator boot camp. All Women Are Lustful: She seems very obsessed with sex, and quite fond of threesomes. Amazonian Beauty: She's aLadettewith a muscular physique, as good a fighter as any of the men and it alsoserves to heighten her attractiveness. Amicable Exes:Although she seems a bit upset, she is cordial to Gannicus when he leaves her for Sibyl, though she makes a point of stating she thinks he'll "ruin" her with his ways and then come back to her anyway. It's made clear they still care about each other, especially in their final scene together.

characters.name: Lugo
characters.description: Lugo is a Germanic warrior captured by Romans and transported to Neapolis as a slave. He later becomes a strong rebel warrior under Spartacus' command. The Big Guy: Played with. He is actually one of the shortest rebelsas well as one of the strongest and most muscular. Boisterous Bruiser: Played straight. Deadpan Snarker: Largely directed at Nasir, e.g. "Wake me when trees attack, little man". Dying Moment of Awesome:Continues slaying Romans despite managing to survive a near impact of a ballista shot and constantly burning away. When two Romans finally get him in the back he screams "f*ck your mothers!".

characters.name: Donar
characters.description: Donar is a former gladiator from Batiatus' Ludus. He escapes with Spartacus following the revolt, and becomes one of the top warriors among the rebellion's ranks. Better to Die than Be Killed: Hedrives his sword up throughhis own headto cheat Caesar out of executing him. The Big Guy: He is stronger and larger than Lugo, making himtheBig Guy of Spartacus army. Dead Guy on Display:Crassus crucifies his corpse for Spartacus to see. Deadpan Snarker. Many of of the things he says.

characters.name: Nemetes
characters.description: Nemetes is a Germanic warrior captured by Romans and transported to Neapolis as a slave. He becomes a prominent but restless rebel under Spartacus' command. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Hegoes down trying to make a deal with Caesar to backstab Spartacus. Caesar isn't buying it. Battle Couple: With Saxa, until hisKick the Dog(see below) actions inVengeancecause her to dump him in disgust. Dirty Coward: When the tables turn, Nemetes will sell out anyone to save his own hide. If You're So Evil, Eat This Kitten!: His idea of getting Caesar to prove his loyalty is demanding that he rape and torture a Roman prisoner.

characters.name: Sedullus
characters.description: Sedullus is a Germanic warrior captured by Romans and transported to Neapolis as a slave. He serves as the alpha male of his Germanic brethren. Blood Knight: His "cock hardens at the fucking thought" of killing Romans and he winds up starting a huge fight between the rebels. The Giant: He is portrayed by the tallest actor in the series, standing around 7ft tall. Gratuitous German: Primarily speaks this. Jerkass: He starts to seem like aJerk with a Heart of Goldafter he engages Naevia in friendly conversation and offers her wine...only to swiftly be revealed as aJerk with a Heart of Jerkwhen heattempts to rape her and then attacks Agron when he tries to intervene.

characters.name: Sibyl
characters.description: Sibyl is a young and beautiful Greek slave, rescued from Roman enslavement by Gannicus and the rebels inWar of the Damned. Now free, she wants a glimpse of affection from her savior. Action Survivor: She's not very good at fighting, though she survives a number of potentially deadly situations and at least tries to fight back againstHeracleoand her dominus. Age-Gap Romance: Gannicus is a hardened gladiator and warrior by the time they meet, and she's considered very young, barely even a woman. While there is only a six year age gap between Gwendoline Taylor and Dustin Claire, Sibyl is clearly intended to be younger than her actress's age of 25 (according to Gwendoline Taylor, she's 20). All Girls Want Bad Boys: Subverted; she falls head over heels forGannicus, but seems to love him because she views him as a heroic man whosaved her life and liberated her. All-Loving Heroine: She's a very kind and caring person, even towards some of the Romans; she's seen handing out food to the Roman prisoners, is kind to Laeta and risks her own life to help rescue herfrom Heracleo.

characters.name: Castus
characters.description: Castus is a Numidian pirate and the right-hand man of Heracleo. He later joins the rebellion after his allies' betrayal. Adaptational Late Appearance: He's part of Spartacus'Elite Fourgeneralsin real life. Here he didn't appear until the final season since Agron already got his characterization. Borrowed Catchphrase: While watching Nasir fight in make-shift arena, he borrows Agron's "fuck the gods". Can't Hold His Liquor: Becomes an important plot point:due to passing out drunk, the pirates leave him behind and so he is not involved with their betrayal of the rebels, ultimately joining them. The Charmer: Especially to Nasir. Unfortunately for him, whilst Nasir is flattered, he only has eyes for Agron.

characters.name: Diotimos
characters.description: Diotimos is a former slave of Laurus who escaped and became a rebel in Spartacus' army. Action Survivor: He tries to learn some fighting skills from Naevia butgets killed in the same episode. Character Death:When the rebels take Sinuessa. Due to the Dead:One of the fallen characters honored inThe Dead and the Dying. In the Back:Laurus stabs him in the back of the neck whilst he's trying to rescue his fellow slaves.

characters.name: Attius
characters.description: Attius is a Roman and a blacksmith in Sinuessa en Valle. He is a friend of Gannicus, whom he met when the latter gained his freedom. Action Survivor: He makes swords rather than wield them, but can still hold his own well enough.He's no match forNaevia, though. Forgotten Fallen Friend:One of the few fallen characters who wasn't honored inThe Dead and the Dying. The Mole:Averted, but doesn't help him against an insane Naevia. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished:Hisvocal disapproval of the rebel's treatment of their captivesis part of what makes Naevia suspicious of him. That, and just being Roman.

characters.name: Heracleo
characters.description: Heracleo is the leader of a band of Cilician Pirates. Adaptation Expansion/Named by the Adaptation: The historical Spartacus allied withand was betrayed/abandoned bypirates, and Heracleo most definitely represents them. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: All the slaves warn Spartacus against trusting him citing his profession of apirate.Turns out that he can be trusted after all as he helps Spartacus beat the Romans in a skirmish. But then he betrays the Rebels after the Romans offer more coin. Devil in Plain Sight: His constant lines about how he's only in it for the money and will betray anyone at the slightest provocation make him come across as aLoveable Roguejokeuntil he actually does sell out Spartacus and the rebellion in exchange for Crassus's money. Early-Bird Cameo: The show'sartistic licensechanges the sequence of events, placing his involvement earlier in the war than is historically accurate.

characters.name: Sanus
characters.description: Sanus is a Cilician rebel who is both a friend and admirer of Gannicus.

characters.name: Belesa
characters.description: A Thracian slave girl first appearing in "Decimation", eventually becoming Saxa's lover. All Women Are Lustful: In her first appearance, she happily bares her breasts to show herSlave Brandto Saxa and Gannicus and states doesn't mind if they touch. She's later shown making out with Saxa in front of everyone. Ambiguously Bi: She is attracted to Saxa for sure, but she also looked at Gannicus in a very flirtatious manner. Bit Character: She only has about three lines, but has a handful of scenes where she's prominent as well as a few background appearances. Bury Your Gays:Averted; she's one of the few surviving rebels in the end.

characters.name: Achillia
characters.description: Achillia, birth name Neferet, is a fierce young Nubian woman. Ashur, looking for an exotic new offering for the gladiatorial games, decides to make her the very first female gladiator. Action Girl: Achillia, a fierce Nubian woman, is trained to be the first female gladiator, with her becoming very skilled. Additionally, she was a warrior even before becoming a gladiatrix, with her being bodyguard to the princess of her kingdom. Amazonian Beauty: While she's still lean, she is very toned, strong and is considered beautiful by other characters such as Celadus and eventually Tarchon. Pompey is attracted to her as well. Ambiguously Bi: While she has had passionate love scenes with two men, when she hears about "wine and whores", her phrasing indicates she would have liked to partake in both had she been allowed, as she doesn't ask if there might be men among the whores. Further, before she makes love to Celadus, she draws a distinction that "there are none but men beneath this roof", suggesting she may prefer women. Dark and Troubled Past: There are several indications that Achillia suffered a traumatic past before she was enslaved to the Romans. She has scars on the back of her hand, suggesting past abuse, and experiences brief flashbacks to what looks to be her home being invaded. It's revealed that she was bodyguard to her princess and accidentally killed her while trying to save her from apparent kidnapping, and she was condemned to slavery as an alternate punishment to death.

characters.name: Doctore Korris
characters.description: Korris is a former slave and seasoned gladiator who earned his freedom through his victories in the arena. Despite enjoying life as a free man for years, he has found himself in need of employment and thus has come to work for Ashur as Doctore for his gladiators. As Korris is not a slave, he is on more equal footing with Ashur in terms of social standing, resulting in a more unique and tumultous relationship between Doctore and Dominus than previously seen in the franchise. Badass Teacher: Given he's teaching gladiators, this is pretty much required, and he proves it in by dominating every fight he’s in. Brave Scot: Although he's not stated to be Scottish, GrahamMcTavishplays up a gruff Scottish accent (his own is much more neutral) to sell him as a badass. Brutal Honesty: Often does this, though it gets him into trouble withAshur, who doesn't appreciate him calling him out. Covered with Scars: On his chest and back.

characters.name: Hilara
characters.description: Hilara is the vilica (essentially housekeeper) of Ashur's ludus and his personal body slave. All for Nothing: Hilara realizes that she should have returned Messia's feelings and kisses her, but by that point, Messia's heart is too broken and she's already moved on. All Love Is Unrequited: Hilara is hopelessly in love with Ashur, despite her being a slave in his service. However, it is clear Ashur doesn't care very much for her, and is more focused on Viridia. Eventually, Hilara seems to realize Ashur's flaws and attempts to get together with Messia, whom she had previously rejected. But after Messia rejects her in turn, she falls back into Ashur's arms in the finale. Ambiguously Bi: While she turns down Messia's advances, she merely says that she considers her a friend, and still engages in a threesome with her without visible annoyance and later seems like she's giving it a try when apologising, and seems genuinely saddened when Messia rejects her. Her actress Jamaica Vaughan referred to Hilara as bisexual in an interview, but so far nothing has been confirmed. Evil Redhead: She initially seems that way, as she threatens Achillia with the warning that she could poison her food and drink should she lay hands on Ashur again, but she's shown in a more sympathetic light.

characters.name: Messia
characters.description: Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: In contrast to the red-headed Hilara, who's more open and emotional about her feelings, Messia is typically stoic and composed. Ambiguously Bi: She reveals that she is in love with Hilara and although she has sex with Ashur as part of a threesome, it's ambiguous whether she has an attraction to men or merely does as he commanded. Beautiful Slave Girl: Ashur uses her for his own sexual pleasure, and Cornelia takes a fancy to her as well, while she's gorgeous. Broken Pedestal: She thinks highly of Hilara at first, but soon loses respect for her when she sees how she kowtows to Ashur. Genre Savvy: She can pick up on the attraction between Ashur and Viridia, and urges Hilara to let go of her infatuation.

characters.name: Viridia
characters.description: Viridia is the daughter of Senator Gabinius and Cossutia. She develops an affection for Ashur due to his role in ending Spartacus' life and rebellion, as her husband was killed by the rebel leader during his attack on Sinuessa en Valle. Break the Cutie: Over the course of the season, she sees her love interest, Ashur, kiss another woman, is bullied by herEvil Uncle, loses her father at the hands of Pompey and Ashur, and is increasingly disillusioned with her fellow nobility. Viridia did not do anything to deserve any of it. Daddy's Girl: She's much closer to her father than her mother. Evil Uncle: Viridia has barely restrained hate for her ruthless, cruel uncle. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: In contrast to her mother, who's aBitch in Sheep's Clothing, Viridia's golden hair symbolises that she's a kind-hearted soul. She's also one of the few characters that immediately loves the idea of Achillia fighting in the arena.

characters.name: Celadus
characters.description: One of the more seasoned gladiators of Ashur's ludus and the father of Tarchon.

characters.name: Tarchon
characters.description: Celadus' son and fellow gladiator.

characters.name: Dacus
characters.description: A slave of Ashur tasked with the readying the training equipment of the ludus.

characters.name: Elata
characters.description: Tarchon's lover who works as a prostitute.

characters.name: Quintus Lentulus Batiatus
characters.description: Batiatus is a Lanista, a trainer and trader of gladiators. He is head of his family's ludus in Capua, and is Dominus to Spartacus and most of the other gladiators that appear throughout the series. Batiatus is the son of Titus Lentulus Batiatus, and the husband of Lucretia. Action Survivor: He's not a trained fighter, but can hold his own when he has to and delivers a fewNo-Holds-Barred-Beatdownsin his time. He's no match fora group of trained gladiators, though that doesn't stop him from trying. Adaptation Name Change: The historical Batiatus was named Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus, not Quintus. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: He briefly implores Oenomaeus to help him during the gladiator revolt, only to realize it won't work and instead switches to wrathful defiance. Affably Evil: If you're not on his bad side he's a great host, and he remembers toPet the Dogfrom time to time, like sparing Spartacus' life when he loses to Crixus. He also loves his wife and dreams of being a father. However, cross him, and he will make you suffer.

characters.name: Lucretia
characters.description: Lucretia is a Roman woman of moderate standing in the land of Capua and lives with her husband, Batiatus, in the villa above his ludus. Through her husband's (and to an extent her own) schemes, the couple manage to climb quite high on the social scale, only to fall after Spartacus seeks revenge and rebels. Accidental Murder: InGods of the Arena, sheinadvertently poisons Melitta after she drinks tainted wine, which Lucretia had used to kill Titus. She's actually pretty upset about it, though no one ever learns she was responsible. Achey Scars:Her stomach aches when she sees Crixus after he stabbed her in the gut. All Women Are Lustful: She cheats on Batiatus with Crixus and likes seeing her husband performing sexual acts with their slave as foreplay. She also sleeps with Gaia and the two of them engage in threesomes with her husband. Ambition Is Evil: Her ambition is something she shares with Batiatus; though she tends to be more cautious than him, she's willing to do just about anything to help elevate their status and protect her own position.

characters.name: Ashur
characters.description: Ashur is an ex-gladiator in Batiatus' ludus and due to a conflict with Crixus prior toBlood and Sand, he was crippled and forced to wear a brace on his right leg. Since then, he became Batiatus' errand boy, accompanying him into the city to aid in transactions or sometimes going alone for more private business. When Batiatus is killed, Ashur seeks out Glaber as a new patron to further his own desires. Using his years in the ludus, Ashur seeks to become a link between Spartacus and the Romans who are hunting him. Adaptational Nice Guy: In theAlternate Universe"House of Ashur" spinoff, his few sympathetic and admirable traits are given extra focus whilst his most vile tendencies, such as hisChronic Backstabbing Disorderand abuse towards women, are downplayed if not outright ignored. While he is still prone to losing his temper and is not above killing a useful slave when enraged, Ashur does value and reward the loyalty of those close to him, such as his Doctore Korris, and treats his female slaves, especially Hilara and Messia, with considerable respect. He is also genuinely smitten with Viridia, is prone to acting bashful when speaking with her, goes out of his way to protect her, yet restrains from actively courting her because of his low standing and fearing her parents' reactions.Steven DeKnight states that this is purposeful, as the series is meant to show that there is still some of the old Ashur who wanted to be part of the brotherhood despite all the humiliation and that now that he is in a position of power and actually has a chance to form genuine bonds with others, he is starting to rediscover parts of his humanity. Arch-Enemy: To Crixus. Well, he considers Crixus his archenemy. Crixus, while contemptuous of him, doesn'tshare the feeling. Until he finds out that Ashur took Naevia against her will, that is. Asshole Victim: He fully deservesgetting decapitated by Naevia afterwhat he did to herand for the suffering he caused many others. Bad Boss: He murders a

characters.name: Ilithyia
characters.description: Ilithyia is a wealthy Roman woman, the daughter of Senator Albinius, and the wife of Praetor Gaius Claudius Glaber. She is close friends with Lucretia, however, their lively relationship is more than meets the eye. All Women Are Lustful: Ilithyialovessex, both for her own enjoyment as well as to manipulate others. It's pretty much her go-to response in absolutely any scenario. Alpha Bitch: Starts the series as aself-absorbed,Spoiled Bratwho's primarily interested in her own amusement.She only gets worse from there. Ambiguously Bi: She does kiss Lucretia on the lips more than once, but at least one of those was a"Take That!" Kiss, and she only ever shows an attraction to men throughout the series. Awful Wedded Life: InVengeanceher marriage to Glaber becomes increasingly unhappy to the point that she plots to divorce him and marry Varinius. Unfortunately, Glaber finds out, quickly nixes that plan, and then proceeds to make her lifenigh-unbearable. He's so awful to her that some viewers actually found themselves feelingsorryfor Ilithyia even though she's generally horrid and brought some of it on herself.

characters.name: Gaius Claudius Glaber
characters.description: Glaber is a Roman commander awarded the title of Legatus and later Praetor. He is married to Senator Albinius's favored daughter, Ilithyia, who supports her husband's actions politically and emotionally, by personally seeing to it that Glaber's greatest enemy, Spartacus, suffers as much pain as possible. Glaber serves as the main antagonist for the second season of Spartacus, and in the first season is a personal antagonist for Spartacus himself as Glaber enslaved both him and his wife Sura. Arch-Enemy: To Spartacus. Interestingly, he doesn't see Spartacus the same way until he starts projecting all his problems onto the man. Asshole Victim: Given his status as asociopathicsadistwho murders anyone who slights him and derives pleasure from doing so, his deathat the hands of Spartacus, whom he taunted viatelling him about his wife's likely multiple rapes as a slavewhen he had the upper hand,isn't meant to evoke sympathy or sadness from the viewers. Attack the Mouth:On the receiving end of it, courtesy of Spartacus thrusting a sword through his mouthto stop him from taunting Spartacus any more than he already has beenin hisDefiant to the Endmoment. Awful Wedded Life: Zigzagged. At first, he and Illythia are very happy together, but Glaber is furious at her murder of Licinia and Batiatus's ensuing blackmail. Things sour heavily between them as Glaber's fortunes dwindle and he learns Illythia plans to divorce him. He sadly asks if there's anything left between them and she remarks that there are only memories to fade. When he kills her father, Glaber snaps and keeps Illythia married to him simply to torture her as much as possible, coldly throwing her own words back at her when she begs for forgiveness. But then Illythia proves she's just as evil and devious as him and the two reunite to "be monsters together."

characters.name: Albinius
characters.description: Albinius is a Roman Senator and father of Ilithyia. He plays a minor role throughout the series, although his role increases inVengeance. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: He begs Glaber to save him in the collapse of the arena. Glaber is not inclined to mercy thanks to Albinius's mistreatment of him. Corrupt Politician: Clearly wields a lot of influence in the Senate, and uses it in the grand tradition of Roman patronage to advance those he personally favors (e.g. Varinius) and cut down those he does not (e.g. Glaber). Doting Parent: It's made clear he genuinely loves his daughter and gives her almost anything she asks for. Unfortunately, him spoiling Ilithyia all her life is probablyone of the main reasons she's such a horrible person. Entitled Bastard: InVengeance,he asked Glaber for help after he was pinned by the debris of the collapsing arena. Prior to this, he insulted and mocked Glabernumerous times, and rubbed it in his face that he was going to let Ilithyia divorce him. Glaber's response?Glaber:"I'm not the fool you and your daughter think me! (CueOh, Crap!)

characters.name: Marcus Decius Solonius
characters.description: Marcus Decius Solonius is a Lanista of Capua and is Batiatus' nemesis and chief rival. All Love Is Unrequited: It's implied that he has feelings for Lucretia. Even after his friendship with Batiatus fell apart, he was always very polite and amicable to Lucretia, and alsoswoops in to save herfrom embarrassing social situations. This was even evident inGods of the Arena, as when Batiatus reveals his father wants him to dissolve his marriage, Solonius seemsveryinterested all of a sudden, and he later offers to let Lucretia shelter in his home if Batiatus' plan against Tullius goes awry...as a "friend", of course. Condemned Contestant: He's sent to face Spartacus in the arena, a death sentence. Cool Old Guy: He is old, incredibly ripped,and puts up a good fight against Spartacus. Defiant to the End: Rather than accepting his fate, he fightsSpartacus knowing he had no chance of coming out alive.

characters.name: Licinia
characters.description: Licinia is an upper-class Roman, married without kids, cousin to the wealthy Marcus Crassus, and a close friend of Ilithyia. All Women Are Lustful: She pays Batiatus and Lucretia for sex with Spartacus. Asshole Victim:Given she helps facilitate rape by fraud in the hopes of ruining a rival, no one's particularly sad about her getting a concrete sandwich, and they're more concerned with the repercussions of a woman of her status being killed in their house. Alpha Bitch: She can almost out-bitchIlithyiawith her snide remarks andBackhandedCompliments. Bait the Dog: She actually seems more like aLovable Alpha Bitchearly on, finding Spartacus speaking out of turn to IlithyiaActually Pretty Funnyand being friendly to Lucretia. Then she takes part in theBed Trickand delights in telling Ilithyia how "will this not seteverytongue in Rome wagging". Ilithyia did warn Lucretia that she did like to play games on her social inferiors.

characters.name: Titus Calavius
characters.description: Calavius is a high-standing Roman Magistrate, husband of Domitia, and proud father of Numerius. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Batiatus bends over backwards to accommodate him, in the hopes he will help him with his political ambitions. It's all for nothing as Calavius discourages him from reaching above his station. Defiant to the End:After being kidnapped by Batiatus and being at his mercy, he retorts with aThe Reason You SuckSpeech. Slashed Throat:How he dies courtesy of Ashur, and Solonius gets framed for his murder.

characters.name: Numerius Calavius
characters.description: Numerius is the son of Roman Magistrate Titus Calavius and his wife, Domitia Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: At first he seems like a nice enough kid, perhaps a little too thrilled by watching people kill each other, but hey,Values Dissonance, right? He worships the ground Spartacus walks on and treats him with admiration, even though he's a slave, so he can't be all bad.Then he orders Spartacus to kill Varro, his best friend. Ok, he was manipulated into it by Illythia, just a dumb kid mesmerized by a nice pair of tits, right? Wrong. When confronted about Varro's death by Aurelia, he coldly says that "He was nothing. He deserved to die." However nice this kid might seem, he serves as perhaps the coldest reminder that to the Roman Elite, slaves are nothing but playthings to be discarded on a whim. Broken Pedestal: Inverted with Spartacus. He idolizes the champion gladiator and Spartacus, in return, was quite fond of him. But after heordered Varro's death, Spartacus has openly expressed his disdain for him. Karmic Death:Ordering a gladiator's death? Get viciously stabbed to death by his wife later on. Non-Action Guy: He's a physically weak kid who can just run from a fight.

characters.name: Aulus
characters.description: Aulus is Batiatus' 'handyman', doing whatever errand or dirty work he requests. Chekhov's Gunman: He's not just a simple "handyman", he isthe one who spilled the beans to Spartacus regarding Sura's murder, thus kickstarting theGladiator Revolt. Hero Killer:Killed Sura, by orders of Batiatus.

characters.name: Mecato
characters.description: Mercato is a Roman politician and noble of Capua. He is the grandson of Marcus Minucius Rufus, famed conqueror of the Thracians. Canon Foreigner: Possibly not. His aforementioned grandfather did exist in real life.

characters.name: Theokoles
characters.description: Theokoles was a legendary Greek gladiator and was also known as the Shadow of Death. Anti-Hero/Anti-Villain: His origin story,as related in the prequel motion comic, paints him more as one of these. Defeating the Undefeatable: On both sides in fact. He's famed for having killed 100 men by himself, and he later ends up on the receiving end of this by Spartacus and Crixus. Dented Iron: By the time Spartacus and Crixus fight him, his body is essentially a mass of scar tissue, and he's been retired for several years. If his fight with Oenomeus in the prequel comic is anything to go by, during his prime he was likely the single most dangerous fighter within series canon. Disappeared Dad: Had one; supposedly a Spartan soldier.

characters.name: Gaia
characters.description: Gaia is a recently widowed Roman woman of Capua and close childhood friend of Lucretia. The Alcoholic: She drinks almost as much asGannicus. All Women Are Lustful: The woman is lust personified. Anti-Villain:Well-Intentioned Anti-Villain. Most of her more malevolent acts (such aslying, cheatingandscrewing around) are to help her friends Lucretia and Quintus achieve their goals, whilst she appearsutterly obliviousto how she may unintentionally hurt her slaves. Benevolent Boss:Zig-Zagged. She is usuallykind to her slaves, even speaking with them like equals on occasion, but she's also rather oblivious to abuses committed against them, a notable example is the incident withGannicus and Melitta- she seems not to notice or care about their discomfort in them being forced to have sex for her and her companions' amusement.

characters.name: Titus Lentulus Batiatus
characters.description: Titus Lentulus Batiatus is the father of Quintus Lentulus Batiatus and Paterfamilias (head) of The House of Batiatus inGods of the Arena. Anti-Villain:Well-Intentioned. He's a lotnicerand morereasonablethan many of the other Roman elites in the series, especially compared to his son, and only behaves harshlyif he feels it necessaryto restore peace and order. Benevolent Boss: He is shown to be well-loved by his slaves. Oenomaus' flashbacks inVengeancealso shows this. Of course, this is relative to other bosses who have slaves fight to the death for entertainment and profit. The difference seems to be that he doesn'trapethem, nor does he send them tothe mineswithout provocation. Blood from the Mouth:Due to being poisoned. Defiant to the End:Wascrawlingafter Lucretia while the poison he has is taking effect and even tries to strangle her.

characters.name: Tullius
characters.description: Tullius is a rich merchant and former soldier, and sits among the elite Roman class of Capua. Arch-Enemy: To Batiatus. Asshole Victim:He fully deserved to be brutally killed by Batiatus and his gladiators, even if he didn't actually commit the crime they killed him for. Big Bad: InGods of the Arena. He is the primary cause of Batiatus' troubles, ultimately driving a wedge between Batiatus and his father that ends in the latter's death, and his actions ultimately leading to Solonius and Quintus' friendship fracturing as well. Say what you will about most of the other Roman elite, but at least most of them never brutally murdered fellow Romans for the sheer giggling spite of it. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He seems like aReasonable Authority Figureand a fairly affable guy at first...but swiftly reveals his true colors by murdering Batiatus's bodyguard and having him beaten to a pulp and humiliatedfor refusing to sell him Gannicus.

characters.name: Vetius
characters.description: Vettius is a young lanista in Capua. The Dragon: To Tullius. The Exile:Was forced to be this due to his deal with Solonius. Karma Houdini:Averted. His life is spared but at the cost of giving his ludus and all his gladiators to Solonius, and leaving Capua. So he literally loses everything except his life. Kick Them While They Are Down:Does this to Batiatus. Batiatus has Ashur return the favour.

characters.name: Quinctilius Varus
characters.description: Quinctilius Varus is a Roman of high social standing. Canon Foreigner: One of a few different characters that is not a singular analogue to a historical person, but rather likely derived from multiple sources. Depraved Homosexual: Gaia's hinting towards his perversions makes it sound as though she'll seduce him to Batiatus' and Lucretia's favor. To everyone's surprise, it turns out he prefers men and has an eye for Gannicus, and he takes his time admiring the latterveryclosely. Eerie Pale-Skinned Brunette: A trait of his that sticks out, as his hair is much darker than the average Roman's. Karma Houdini: Never gets any comeuppance for essentially having slaves sexually abused. Like Gaia, it doesn't seem like he notices or cares about Gannicus' obvious discomfort, nor Melitta's.

characters.name: Cossutius
characters.description: Cossutius is a Roman of high social standing and a close friend of Varus. All Men Are Perverts: But none hold a candle to him, as he is the biggest pervert in the series. The Bus Came Back: InVengeance.Back for the Dead: With a very strong dose ofAsshole Victimthrown in. Back for the Dead: With a very strong dose ofAsshole Victimthrown in. But for Me, It Was Tuesday: Somewhat. He apparently recognizes the slave he had raped at her execution, but does not remember her name.

characters.name: Caburus
characters.description: Caburus is a mighty gladiator and champion of the House of Vettius and later the House of Solonius. he is despised by professional gladiators and lanista because he is purposely matched against smaller and weaker gladiators. And Show It to You: His first fight ends with him ripping his opponent's heart out. Big Bad: Acts as one for the arena.The Brute Blood Knight: Seems to take a special and sadistic glee from killing other gladiators. The Bully: His opponents are usually smaller and weaker than him. Though admittedly, he didn't choose them.

characters.name: Publius Varinius
characters.description: Publius Varinius is a high-ranking Praetor in the Roman Senate. His power and influence rivals Glaber’s own, causing much friction between the two as Varinius seeks to use Spartacus' rebellion as a way to gain favor for himself in the Republic, and knows that catching Spartacus would bring him glory. Chick Magnet: He's regarded as very handsome and has both Ilithyia and Seppia vying for his affections. Composite Character: Possibly. Sources differ on whether there were two Roman generals "Publius"and"Varinius", or a single "Publius Varinius". Death by Adaptation:Historical records indicate that Varinius survived the war, though "was nearly captured". In the show, he gets killed in the final episode ofVengeance. Death by Disfigurement:Gets half his face scorched off by the impact of a flaming catapult stone.

characters.name: Seppius
characters.description: Seppius is a young Roman noble and older brother of Seppia. InVengeance, he leads a local militia intent on capturing Spartacus. Blood from the Mouth: On the nightGlaber murders him. Brother–Sister Incest: He'simplied to be attracted to his sister. He's overprotective of her to the point he seemsjealousof other men who show attraction to his sister and doesn't pretend to be sad when Seppia loses Varinius' affections. He's also very touchy-feely with her, even kissing her full on the mouth. Chekhov's Gun: His bracelet.Ashur takes it from him when he and his men massacre his household on Glaber's orders. Lucretia later finds the bracelet in Ashur's box of loot and uses it to reveal to Seppia that it was really Glaber who murdered her brother. The Unfought: He's set up as a major opponent of Spartacus and his rebels, due to his wealth enabling him to hire soldiers to hunt them down, but ultimately Spartacus never comes to face-to-face with Seppius himselfas he's murdered by Glaber, who thenpins it on the rebels.

characters.name: Seppia
characters.description: Seppia is the beautiful younger sister of Seppius, whose youthful innocence hides a much more cunning and devious nature. Alpha Bitch: Acts very much like the Roman equivalent. She's quite spoilt and insensitive, thinking nothing of making snide comments about other women and can be a bit manipulative (though she'snot remotely in the same leagueas Ilithyia and Lucretia). Anti-Villain: She's not reallyevil, just very self-absorbed. And considering she's up against the likes ofLucretiaandIlithyia... Even Evil Has Loved Ones: She may be a selfish brat, but it's clear she genuinely loves her brother, Seppius.She's utterly distraught when he's murdered and vows revenge on his killer. Even Evil Has Standards: Gets horrified when the Roman Elite are stabbing and mutilating a helpless slaveFor the Evulz.

characters.name: The Egyptian
characters.description: The Egyptian is a mysterious character who works as a member of Ashur's Group. Beware the Quiet Ones: We almost never hear him speak yet is feared by many around him. The Brute: He's a vicious, physical threat who simply mows down all in his path. Dark and Troubled Past: According tothe creators and his actor, the Egyptian was a soldier during Egypt's civil war and lost his family there. The Dragon: The Egyptian is Ashur's top warrior. Unfortunately, as a mercenary, he's not exactly loyal. When Glaber offers him more money, he abandons Ashur without a second thought.

characters.name: Marcus
characters.description: Marcus is the Military Tribune of Gaius Claudius Glaber. Attack! Attack! Attack!: Unfortunately for him, it doesn't work as expected. Badass Normal: Gets into not one but two swordfights with Spartacus without being killed instantly. Bad Boss: By the end of episode 4, you'd be forgiven for thinking that hewantshis men to all get killed. Defiant to the End: He angrily rebukes Ashur for abandoning the mission, leading to his death.

characters.name: Salvius
characters.description: Salvius is a soldier, and later Tribune, serving under Glaber. Butt-Monkey: Him getting beaten up by various characters verges on aRunning Joke. Also, despite being an experienced soldier who handles most of the army logistics and demonstratesUndying Loyaltyto his commander, he gets sidelined by said commander in favor of aSmug Snakeslave. Hero Killer: Kills Mira with a thrown axe, although his intended target was Spartacus. Nevertheless, this still makes him the only Roman to kill a significant member of the rebellion inVengeance. Interrupted Intimacy: You've got to admire his poker face when he walks in onGlaber cheating on his wife with Seppia, to report the kidnapping of said wife no less. Mook Lieutenant: Takes over this role after Marcus is killed.

characters.name: Marcus Licinius Crassus
characters.description: Marcus Licinius Crassus is the richest man in Rome and a senator of the Republic. Envied and despised by the highborn among the Senate, he craves the power and respect that defeating Spartacus and his rebel army would bring him. Abusive Parents: A large part of why Tiberius is asmessed up as he isstems from the way Crassus force feeds him contradictory lessons about how important it is to be honorable yet ruthless, obedient yet self-serving and loyal but willing to kill those you are loyal to. The Ace: Crassus is rich, politically powerful, highly intelligent, has a firm grasp of military strategy, personal combat and is capable of accepting minor losses in the present for a better position in the future. He is the quintessential RomanRenaissance Man. Action Dad: To both his sons, but particularly Tiberius, who he takes with him on his campaign against Spartacus. Affably Evil: Genuinely nice to his slaves, generally charming and polite but also a scheming politician and a brutal fighter. Is not so much evil as a firm believer ofI Did What I Had to Do.

characters.name: Gaius Julius Caesar
characters.description: Julius Caesar is a young rogue from an esteemed lineage. He will join along side with Marcus Licinius Crassus as the devoted antagonist. His deadly intelligence and leadership will be brought to bear against the rebellion as he begins his ascent towards the all-powerful ruler he will one day become. Adaptational Villainy: He'sThe DragontoBig BadCrassus, thoughin real life, there's little evidence he was eveninvolvedwith the Third Servile War. Adaptation Dye-Job: He's blond. The real life Caesar is/was famously anEerie Pale-Skinned Brunette. Anti-Villain: Generally a Noble Anti-Villain, though averted when dealing with the rebels,whom he enjoys killing. Animal Motifs: Everyone describes him as a wolf, and it is his emblem.

characters.name: Tiberius Licinius Crassus
characters.description: Tiberius is the son of Marcus Licinius Crassus. He is given the duty of defeating Spartacus and his army along with Crassus, and is using this opportunity to please and gain favor from his father by doing so. Adaptation Name Change: The real Marcus Crassus' oldest son was also namedMarcus Licinius (kinda like a Jr.), not Tiberius. A Death in the Limelight:In an unsympathetic kind of way. Age Lift: His real life counterpart is around 15 by the time of the Third Servile War. To be a soldier, one should be at least 17 years old. Ambiguously Bi: Him and Sabinus are seeminglyJust Friends, but the latter is hisMorality Petand they have several held gazes. Although herapes Kore, he also does the same to Caesar. His actor says that they weren't lovers, but that doesn't mean there wasn't an attraction. In fact, his rape of Kore was specifically said to be his idea of anEquivalent Exchangefor losing Sabinus, and later episodes make it clear he knew she and his father were in love.

characters.name: Kore
characters.description: Kore is a slave to the Crassus family. She has been serving Crassus since Tiberius's birth and in many ways is seen as a mother figure. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She's usually quite reserved and professional in public, though she's much friendlier around Crassus and Tiberius. Anti-Villain:Villain In Name Only. She'sa loyal slave to the House of Crassus, is generallya nice personand never really does anything very villainous (or at least not to people who didn't deserve it). Beautiful Slave Girl: Played with. She fits the trope, but exclusively has sex with Crassus, whom she genuinely loves. Betty and Veronica: She's the Betty (Closer to Earthand soft-spoken) to Tertulla's Veronica (pampered and forward), with Crassus as Archie.

characters.name: Laeta
characters.description: Laeta is the privileged wife of a Roman dignitary, who becomes entangled in the struggle against Spartacus. Her life and those of the ones she loves are forever changed by the conflict. Action Survivor: Downplayed. She's not really a fighter, though she manages to killHeracleoand also escapesthe Romanson horseback despite being wounded. Age-Gap Romance: With her late husband. She was onlytwelvewhen she was married off to him and he seems a few decades older than her. All Love Is Unrequited: Downplayed.While Spartacus did return her feelings, it's not in the same amount that he showed Mira and, obviously, Sura. She doesn't seem that bothered, either; unlike Mira, she doesn't seem to resent that Spartacus does not fully return her love and does not push him to show her more intimacy. Anti-Villain:Villain in Name Only.She is a Roman but not evil in the slightest. In fact, she's a great deal more kind and moral than a lot ofthe rebelsby this point in the story. About the only nasty thing she does is threaten Sibyl to not reveal that she's hiding people under the stable, and call her a "rebellious slave" when she does.

characters.name: Tertulla
characters.description: Tertulla is a wealthy Roman woman and the prestigious wife of Marcus Licinius Crassus. The couple had two sons; Tiberius and Publius. Alpha Bitch: Downplayed. She's actually pretty civil for a woman whose husband has been openly cheating on her for well over a decade. Betty and Veronica: The Veronica to Kore's Betty, with Crassus as the Archie. Played with in the sense that it's a loveless marriage.Given Kore's crucifixion in the finale, she technically wins and gets a husband who won't be having an affair anymore. Downplayed Trope: Compared to the female Roman nobles such as Illithyia, Lucretia, Licinia, Seppia, and even Gaia, she's pretty tame. Hero of Another Story: She actually had an affair with Caesar in real life that her husband knew about and is rumoured to have encouraged it to strengthen their political alliance with him. Cicero also slandered her repeatedly, suggesting that both her children were fathered by a different man, since they resembled her friend Quintus Axius. This is not the case in the show, since Tiberius clearly looks like his father.

characters.name: Metellus
characters.description: Metellus is a senator of Rome. He represents the Senate in his political affairs and quickly wishes to see an end to the rebellion.

characters.name: Sabinus
characters.description: Sabinus is a Roman soldier working for Marcus Licinius Crassus and a childhood friend of his son Tiberius. Ambiguously Gay: His interactions with Tiberius borders on massiveHomoerotic Subtext. They're merely said to be friends, but his death haunts Tiberius rather likeThe Lost Lenore. Anti-Villain: He's not a mean or cruel guy, and it was largely Sabinus that kept Tiberius from expressing his more sadistic tendencies. With his death, all bets are off. Canon Foreigner: Since Marcus Crassus's oldest son was too young to have served in the Third Servile War, Sabinus is a completely fictional character. Death by Disfigurement:Was killed via Decimation.

characters.name: Rufus
characters.description: Rufus is one of Crassus' commanders. Demoted to Extra: Historically, he led the army (under Crassus) that defeated, if not killed,Gannicusor/andCastus/Agron. You Shall Not Pass!:Did this against Spartacus.The result is obvious.

characters.name: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus
characters.description: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus is a praetor of Rome, known by many as the "Adolescent Butcher", and "Valiant Pompey". Animal Motifs: His emblem has thedolphinand the eagle, because he is supposedly the master of sea and sky. The Butcher: HisRed Baron. Informed Ability: According to Laeta, he's said to be the deadliest warrior in all the Republic. Which may well be true, but given that we never see him in combat, it's impossible to know. Last Episode, New Character: Makes his appearance after theFinal Battle, stealing credit from Crassus and Caesar over Spartacus' defeat.

characters.name: Laurus
characters.description: A Roman public speaker in Sinuessa and the dominus of several slaves, including Sibyl and Diotimos (until the latter escaped). Asshole Victim/Karmic Death: Gets killed by Gannicus in the middle of threatening his long-suffering slaves. Bad Boss: To all his slaves. Even Laeta thinks so. Diagonal Cut: Gannicus kills in him this manner, slicing his head in two. Establishing Character Moment: His involves him sentencing one of his slaves who had tried to escape topublic execution by stoning, and rallying the crowds to join in and make him suffer as much as possible.

characters.name: Senator Gabinius
characters.description: Gabinius is a Roman Senator based in Capua who holds considerable influence in Rome and oversees the gladiatorial games in Capua. He is a staunch ally of Gnaeus Pompeius "Pompey" Magnus, and spends much of his time working to diffuse the tensions between Pompey and his co-consul, Marcus Crassus. To this end, he enters a tentative partnership with Ashur, who Crassus patrons, hoping the Syrian may be of help in repairing the consuls' relationship. He is the husband of Cossutia and the father of Veridia. Reasonable Authority Figure: Gabinius is one of the only high-status Romans we meet in the series who doesn't obsessively claw for more wealth and power. His primary concern is to ensure the quarrel between Crassus and Pompey is resolved to avoid a civil war. He is also one of the only Romans who treats Ashur with decency, recognizing his potential as an asset and keenly aware that screwing with Ashur too much could invoke the wrath ofCrassus himself.

characters.name: Cornelia
characters.description: Cornelia is the wife of Gaius Julius Caesar and a member of the prominent Cinna family of Rome. Alpha Bitch: One who could put the likes of Ilithyia and evenLicinato shame, difficult as that may be to believe. She is utterly self-absorbed, spoiled, cruel, entitled, cares only about flaunting her status and satisfying her desires, and cannot seem to go more than two sentences without complaining about the lacking standards of others around her. Depraved Bisexual: Cornelia is openly bisexual, frequently indulging in male and female slaves to slake her appetites. She goes to far as assaulting Cossutia (to the older woman’s discomfort) while the two are indulging in sex with Ashur’s gladiators. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: She genuinely loves her husband Caesar, the two constantly showing affection for one another and speaking of him with nothing but regard, a noticeable contrast to the disregard she shows others, which includes her sexually assaulting people and arranging their murders. Queer Establishing Moment: In "Goddess of Death" Cornelia turns out to be into women through having Messia give her cunnilingus. Caesar is well aware of this and indulges her.

characters.name: Cossutia
characters.description: Even Evil Has Loved Ones: She may be snobbish, cruel and spiteful but she does truly love her daughter Viridia and her husband Gabinius. She was also very close friends with Opiter andwas devastated when he died, even asking her husband to host games in his honour. Mama Bear: Towards her daughter, Viridia. Whenthey're both attacked she doesn't hesitate to leap to her daughter's defence, even though she's an ageing patrician woman with a single sword against several mercenaries. Ungrateful Bastard: Even though Ashur saved her life from an attack by Cilician pirates (actually Caesar's men), she still views him with contempt, even laughing when Cornelia humiliates him.

characters.name: Proculus
characters.description: Bad Boss: He blames Satyrus entirely for the facthe fell for Ashur and Cossutia's schemes and lost 5 of his men in the ambush. He then tries to have the dwarf executed by placing him in a match with a gladiator twice his size. Not Me This Time: When Korris is attacked both himself and Ashur assume it was Proculus.Turns out it was actually Cossutia Entitled Bastard: He truly expects Ashur to go into business with him when his fortune improves despite Proculus insulting and scheming against him at every turn. Ashur himself scoffs at the mans entitlement. Smug Snake: He's a very self-satisfied man and he has a very high opinion of himself. So much so he feels free to threaten Cossutia despite the fact she's aristocracy and he's a lanista (which is a profession thats amongst the lowest ranking in status in Roman culture).
